title_en: Ministry of Transport, South China Sea Rescue Bureau v. Archangelos Investment Company and Hong Kong Anda Osen Co., Ltd., Shanghai Representative Office — dispute over maritime salvage contract
ruling_gist_en: The parties to a marine salvage contract expressly agreed that the investment company shall pay remuneration regardless of whether the salvage is successful, and the remuneration is calculated based on standards such as the salvage vessel's horsepower per hour and labor input. Such a salvage contract is not a 'no cure, no pay' salvage contract as stipulated in the International Convention on Salvage 1989 and the Maritime Code, but is an employment salvage contract. Where both the International Convention on Salvage 1989 and the Maritime Code permit the parties to separately agree on the determination of salvage remuneration, yet there are no specific provisions on employment salvage contracts, the relevant provisions of the Contract Law shall apply to determine the rights and obligations of the parties.

full_text_en:
Transportation Ministry of the People's Republic of China Nanhai Rescue Bureau v. Archangelos Investments E.N.E. and Hong Kong Anda Ousen Co., Ltd., Shanghai Representative Office — Dispute over a Salvage Contract

Ruling Summary

Where the parties to a salvage contract expressly agree that, regardless of whether the salvage operation is successful, the investment company shall pay remuneration, and the remuneration is calculated based on factors such as the salvaging vessel's horsepower per hour and manpower input, such a contract does not constitute a "no cure, no pay" salvage contract under the *International Convention on Salvage 1989* or the *Maritime Code of the People's Republic of China*, but rather an employment salvage contract. Since the *International Convention on Salvage 1989* and the *Maritime Code* both permit the parties to separately agree on the determination of salvage remuneration, and there are no specific provisions on employment salvage contracts, the relevant provisions of the *Contract Law* shall apply to determine the rights and obligations of the parties.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

(2016) Zui Gao Fa Min Zai No. 61

Applicant for Retrial (Plaintiff at First Instance, Respondent at Second Instance): Transportation Ministry of the People's Republic of China Nanhai Rescue Bureau. Domicile: No. 42, Binjiang West Road, Haizhu District, Guangzhou City, Guangdong Province, People's Republic of China.

Legal Representative: Lin Zhihao, Director of the Bureau.

Agent ad litem: Wan Renshan, Attorney at Shanghai Chuangyuan Law Firm.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance): Archangelos Investments E.N.E. Domicile: 29 Drossopoulou Street, 11257 Athens, Greece.

Representative: George Balabanos, Chairman of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Huang Hui, Attorney at Guangdong Hengyun Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Zhang Jing, Attorney at Guangdong Hengyun Law Firm.

Defendant at First Instance: Hong Kong Anda Ousen Co., Ltd., Shanghai Representative Office. Domicile: Room 610, Building 1, Jinzhong Tower, No. 680, Zhaojiabang Road, Xuhui District, Shanghai City, People's Republic of China.

Representative: He Xijun, Chief Representative of the Office.

Agent ad litem: Huang Hui, Attorney at Guangdong Hengyun Law Firm.

The applicant for retrial, Transportation Ministry of the People's Republic of China Nanhai Rescue Bureau (hereinafter referred to as Nanhai Rescue Bureau), filed an application for retrial with this Court regarding the dispute over a salvage contract with the respondent Archangelos Investments E.N.E. (hereinafter referred to as Investment Company) and the defendant at first instance Hong Kong Anda Ousen Co., Ltd., Shanghai Representative Office (hereinafter referred to as Shanghai Representative Office), challenging the civil judgment (2014) Yue Gao Fa Min Si Zhong Zi No. 117 rendered by the Guangdong High People's Court (hereinafter referred to as the second instance court). This Court rendered a civil ruling on December 24, 2015, (2015) Min Shen Zi No. 3182, granting the retrial. The case was heard by a collegial panel composed of Vice President and Judge He Rong, Judges Zhang Yongjian, Wang Shumei, Yu Xiaohan, and Acting Judge Guo Zaiyu, and was publicly tried on July 7, 2016. Lin Zhihao, the legal representative of Nanhai Rescue Bureau, and its agent ad litem Wan Renshan; Huang Hui and Zhang Jing, agents ad litem for Investment Company; and Huang Hui, agent ad litem for Shanghai Representative Office, attended the trial. The trial of this case has now been concluded.

Nanhai Rescue Bureau filed a complaint with the Guangzhou Maritime Court (hereinafter referred to as the first instance court), alleging: Investment Company is the owner of the vessel "Archangelos Gabriel," and Shanghai Representative Office is the ship agent of the company. On August 12, 2011, the "Archangelos Gabriel" ran aground in the Qiongzhou Strait. Nanhai Rescue Bureau, upon entrustment by Investment Company, dispatched the vessels "Nanhai Jiu 116," "Nanhai Jiu 101," "Nanhai Jiu 201," and a dive team to the accident site to provide services including salvage, transportation, and standby. According to the agreement between the parties, the total salvage costs incurred amounted to RMB 7,240,998.24 (unless otherwise specified, all amounts below are in RMB), but Investment Company has not paid. The court was requested to: order Investment Company and Shanghai Representative Office to jointly and severally pay Nanhai Rescue Bureau salvage costs of RMB 7,240,998.24; order Investment Company and Shanghai Representative Office to jointly and severally pay Nanhai Rescue Bureau interest for delayed payment from August 20, 2011, until the date of actual payment (calculated at the contemporaneous loan interest rate of the People's Bank of China, the interest amount provisionally calculated to August 19, 2012, being RMB 476,449.64); and order Investment Company and Shanghai Representative Office to jointly and severally bear the litigation costs.

The first instance court found the following facts:

The vessel "Archangelos Gabriel" owned by Investment Company is an oil tanker, with Greece as its flag state and Piraeus as its port of registry, with a gross tonnage of 40,682. The "Archangelos Gabriel" was carrying 54,580 tons of Cabinda crude oil, sailing from Hong Kong to Qinzhou, Guangxi, with a crew of 26 on board. At approximately 0500 hours on August 12, 2011, the vessel ran aground near Buoy No. 6 in the North Channel of the Qiongzhou Strait (at 22 degrees 21 minutes 7.2 seconds north latitude, 110 degrees 48 minutes 7.8 seconds east longitude), with a list of 3 degrees to port. Cracks had appeared in the forepeak tank below the waterline, and seawater had entered the tank. The vessel and its cargo were in a dangerous condition, posing a serious threat to the safety of the marine environment.

After the accident, Investment Company immediately authorized Shanghai Representative Office to send an urgent email to Nanhai Rescue Bureau regarding the grounding of the "Archangelos Gabriel," requesting Nanhai Rescue Bureau to arrange two tugs for salvage based on its experience, and stated that it agreed to Nanhai Rescue Bureau's quotation.

At 2040 hours on August 12, Shanghai Representative Office submitted a letter of authorization to Nanhai Rescue Bureau via email, entrusting Nanhai Rescue Bureau to dispatch the "Nanhai Jiu 116" and "Nanhai Jiu 101" to the site to assist in refloating the "Archangelos Gabriel." It undertook that, regardless of whether the refloating assistance was successful, it agreed to pay at a rate of RMB 3.2 per horsepower per hour, with the billing period commencing from the time of engine preparation of each tug at its respective standby anchorage point until Shanghai Representative Office notified the end of the task and the tug returned to the original standby anchorage point. The "Nanhai Jiu 116" and "Nanhai Jiu 101" were only responsible for towing operations; Nanhai Rescue Bureau was not to be held liable for any accidents occurring during the refloating of the "Archangelos Gabriel." Additionally, Nanhai Rescue Bureau was requested to dispatch a dive team to survey the "Archangelos Gabriel," with costs as follows: land mobilization fee of RMB 10,000; water transportation fee of RMB 55,000; operation fee of RMB 40,000 per 8-hour period, with the billing period commencing from the time the divers boarded the transport vessel and ending when the operation was completed and they left the transport vessel to go ashore.

Simultaneously, in order to prevent further deterioration of the dangerous situation and marine pollution, the Zhanjiang Maritime Safety Administration of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as Zhanjiang MSA) decided to take compulsory lightening and refloating measures for the "Archangelos Gabriel." Organized and arranged by Zhanjiang MSA, on August 17, the vessel "Danchi" owned by China Shipping Development Co., Ltd., Tanker Company, lightered the crude oil from the "Archangelos Gabriel." On August 18, the "Archangelos Gabriel" successfully refloated by utilizing the high tide and then safely arrived at the destination port of Qinzhou, Guangxi. The lightered crude oil was transported to the destination port by the "Danchi."

(1) Work situation of the "Nanhai Jiu 116"

The "Nanhai Jiu 116," owned by Nanhai Rescue Bureau, is a salvage vessel with a gross tonnage of 3,681 and a total power of 9,000 kilowatts (12,240 horsepower). After the "Nanhai Jiu 116" arrived at the accident site, due to Zhanjiang MSA's decision to adopt the lightening and refloating plan, the "Nanhai Jiu 116" did not perform towing salvage on the "Archangelos Gabriel." From 0745 hours on August 12 to 1920 hours on August 18, the vessel stood by the "Archangelos Gabriel" at the accident site in accordance with Investment Company's instructions, working for a total of 155.58 hours. Nanhai Rescue Bureau claimed that, based on the agreed rate of RMB 3.2 per horsepower per hour, Investment Company should pay salvage fees of RMB 6,093,757.44. Investment Company and Shanghai Representative Office argued that they had hired the "Nanhai Jiu 116" and agreed to the rate of RMB 3.2 per horsepower per hour for the purpose of towing operations, but in fact, the vessel only stood by and waited at the site without participating in specific salvage work; therefore, the salvage fees could not be calculated at the originally agreed rate.

(2) Work situation of the "Nanhai Jiu 101"

The "Nanhai Jiu 101," owned by Nanhai Rescue Bureau, is a salvage vessel with a gross tonnage of 4,091 and a total power of 13,860 kilowatts (18,850 horsepower). At 0938 hours on August 12, Nanhai Rescue Bureau sent an email requesting Shanghai Representative Office to confirm the second tug "Nanhai Jiu 101." At 0957 hours, Shanghai Representative Office replied to Nanhai Rescue Bureau, requesting the arrangement of the aforementioned two tugs for salvage.

At 0930 hours on August 12, the "Nanhai Jiu 101" departed for the accident area to salvage the "Archangelos Gabriel." While the vessel was en route to the accident area, Nanhai Rescue Bureau sent an email to Shanghai Representative Office at 1519 hours, stating that, given that the master of the "Archangelos Gabriel" insisted on choosing the lightening method for refloating in accordance with Zhanjiang MSA's opinion, it suggested retaining only the "Nanhai Jiu 116" at the site and having the "Nanhai Jiu 101" return to the anchorage. At 1544 hours, Shanghai Representative Office replied by email, confirming that only the "Nanhai Jiu 116" would be kept at the site and the "Nanhai Jiu 101" was cancelled. At 1550 hours, the vessel began to return and did not reach the accident site; at 2305 hours, it returned to the anchorage. Nanhai Rescue Bureau claimed that the vessel's working time totaled 13.58 hours, and based on the agreed rate of RMB 3.2 per horsepower per hour, Investment Company should pay salvage fees of RMB 819,145.60. Investment Company and Shanghai Representative Office argued that the "Nanhai Jiu 101" returned according to Nanhai Rescue Bureau's instructions while still en route to the accident site and did not actually perform any towing or other operations; thus, calculating fees at the originally agreed rate was manifestly unfair and highly unreasonable.

(3) Work situation of the "Nanhai Jiu 201"

The "Nanhai Jiu 201," owned by Nanhai Rescue Bureau, is a salvage vessel with a gross tonnage of 552 and a total power of 4,480 kilowatts (6,093 horsepower). On August 13, Investment Company proposed chartering the "Nanhai Jiu 201" to transport two of its representatives from Haikou to the "Archangelos Gabriel." Nanhai Rescue Bureau sent an email to Shanghai Representative Office stating that the rate for the "Nanhai Jiu 201" was RMB 1.5 per horsepower per hour, and the total fee would be calculated based on the chartering time. Shanghai Representative Office replied to confirm and agreed, stating that once the two representatives boarded the "Archangelos Gabriel," the "Nanhai Jiu 201" could return to the anchorage.

On August 13, the vessel transported two owner's representatives to board the grounded ship, then returned to the naval dock and finished the engine. The working time for this trip was 7.83 hours.

At 1452 hours on August 15, Shanghai Representative Office sent an email to Nanhai Rescue Bureau, proposing to charter the "Nanhai Jiu 201" on August 16 at 0800 hours to transport relevant personnel and equipment to the "Archangelos Gabriel," and inquired whether the vessel could wait on site for several hours and whether the rate could be set at RMB 1.3 per horsepower per hour. At 1600 hours, Nanhai Rescue Bureau replied that the rate remained RMB 1.5 per horsepower per hour, with the billing period commencing from the time the vessel prepared its engine and left its standby anchorage and ending when the task was completed and the vessel returned to the original standby anchorage and finished its engine. It also stated that the vessel was to be used only as a transport vessel on this trip and was not responsible for assisting with diving survey-related operations. At 2002 hours, Shanghai Representative Office replied that, after difficult negotiations, it agreed to Nanhai Rescue Bureau's plan and requested immediate arrangement.

On August 16, the vessel transported relevant personnel and equipment to the grounded ship, then secured the mooring lines and finished the engine. The working time for this trip was 7.75 hours.

At 1633 hours on August 17, Shanghai Representative Office sent an email to Nanhai Rescue Bureau, proposing a final charter of the "Nanhai Jiu 201" for an operation on August 18, with departure time at 0200 hours on the 18th, to transport the master, surveyors, and others to board the "Archangelos Gabriel." It confirmed the rate at RMB 1.5 per horsepower per hour.

On August 18, the vessel transported relevant personnel and luggage onto the lightering vessel, then secured the bow and stern lines and finished the engine. The working time for this trip was 8.83 hours.

Nanhai Rescue Bureau claimed that, based on the agreed rate of RMB 1.5 per horsepower per hour and 24.41 hours of working time, Investment Company should pay salvage fees of RMB 223,095.20. Investment Company and Shanghai Representative Office argued that the vessel had a total power of 6,093 horsepower, and dispatching such a high-power vessel as a transport vessel constituted taking advantage of the other party's distress to charge excessive fees. Investment Company and Shanghai Representative Office also argued that Nanhai Rescue Bureau had arbitrarily added or deleted entries in the logbook of the "Nanhai Jiu 201," and therefore did not confirm its authenticity; however, Investment Company and Shanghai Representative Office did not provide evidence to support this allegation.

(4) Work situation of the dive team

At 0957 hours on August 12, Shanghai Representative Office sent an email to Nanhai Rescue Bureau, requesting the arrangement of a dive team to survey and confirm the damage and grounding conditions of the "Archangelos Gabriel." At 1554 hours, Shanghai Representative Office sent an email to the ship agent of the "Archangelos Gabriel," Zhanjiang Ocean Shipping Agency Co., Ltd., stating that Nanhai Rescue Bureau's personnel and divers had left the base at approximately 1500 hours and would arrive at the scene at approximately 1730 hours on the same day to conduct underwater survey operations; it entrusted Zhanjiang Ocean Shipping Agency Co., Ltd. to act as the owner's agent, assist Zhanjiang MSA in the salvage, and arrange for the "Archangelos Gabriel" to continue sailing to Qinzhou.

At 1808 hours on August 13, Nanhai Rescue Bureau sent an email to Shanghai Representative Office stating that the dive team boarded the transport vessel at 1500 hours on the 12th and left the transport vessel at 2300 hours on the 12th, with the dive team working for 8 hours, and requested Shanghai Representative Office to confirm. The email also listed the working hours of the "Nanhai Jiu 101" on the 12th and the "Nanhai Jiu 201" on the 13th. At 1935 hours, Shanghai Representative Office replied expressing gratitude for Nanhai Rescue Bureau's efforts, while suggesting that the fees could be slightly reduced, and proposed canceling the operation fees for the "Nanhai Jiu 101" from 0930 to 1530 hours on the 12th, canceling dive operation fees of RMB 100,000, and canceling the fees for the "Nanhai Jiu 201" on the 13th of RMB 55,000. At 2033 hours, Nanhai Rescue Bureau replied that it could not accept the requests in the email.

Nanhai Rescue Bureau claimed that Investment Company and Shanghai Representative Office should pay, as agreed, the land mobilization fee of RMB 10,000, water transportation fee of RMB 55,000, and operation fee of RMB 40,000, totaling RMB 105,000. Investment Company and Shanghai Representative Office argued that the land mobilization fee and water transportation fee already covered the costs of preparing and deploying divers and equipment, and the operation fee of RMB 40,000 per 8 hours should only refer to fees for actual underwater survey operations; since the dive team did not actually perform any underwater survey operations, Nanhai Rescue Bureau was not entitled to charge such fee.

(5) Other facts related to the salvage rates for the "Nanhai Jiu 116" and "Nanhai Jiu 101"

At 1452 hours on August 15, Shanghai Representative Office sent an email to Nanhai Rescue Bureau to negotiate related fees, requesting: 1. Reduce the salvage rate for the "Nanhai Jiu 116" to RMB 2.9 per horsepower per hour. 2. Cancel the charter of the "Nanhai Jiu 101," slightly reduce the charges, and quote the lowest price. 3. Reduce the dive operation fees to RMB 100,000. 4. The fee for chartering the "Nanhai Jiu 201" on the 13th was RMB 55,000. 5. It intended to charter the "Nanhai Jiu 201" on the 16th to transport divers, port captains, and surveyors to board the vessel, and inquired whether the rate could be set at RMB 1.3 per horsepower per hour. At 1600 hours, Nanhai Rescue Bureau replied: the rate for the "Nanhai Jiu 201" remained at RMB 1.5 per horsepower per hour; other fees incurred in the salvage of the "Archangelos Gabriel" would be discussed later.

During the first instance proceedings, Nanhai Rescue Bureau confirmed that Shanghai Representative Office need not bear liability.

The first instance court held:

This case is a dispute over a salvage contract. According to Article 26 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on the Scope of Cases Accepted by Maritime Courts, this case should be under the specialized jurisdiction of a maritime court. The place where the vessel involved in the accident was salved falls within the jurisdiction of the first instance court. Pursuant to Article 31 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the first instance court has jurisdiction over this case.

Since Investment Company is a Greek company and the "Archangelos Gabriel" is a Greek-flagged oil tanker, this case contains foreign-related elements. As all parties chose to apply the laws of the People's Republic of China during the trial, pursuant to Article 3 of the Law of the People's Republic of China on the Application of Laws to Foreign-Related Civil Relations, the laws of the People's Republic of China shall be applied as the governing law for the substantive issues in this case.

(1) Formation and validity of the salvage contract

After the grounding incident, Investment Company's agent, Shanghai Representative Office, sent an email to Nanhai Rescue Bureau requesting the arrangement of two tugs for salvage and stated that it agreed to Nanhai Rescue Bureau's quotation. Additionally, Shanghai Representative Office submitted a letter of authorization to Nanhai Rescue Bureau via email, stipulating the vessels, personnel (divers), and remuneration calculation standards to be used in the salvage. Based on the exchanged emails, it is clear that Investment Company and Shanghai Representative Office were aware of the dangerous condition of the "Archangelos Gabriel" at the time, and Shanghai Representative Office and Nanhai Rescue Bureau had fully discussed issues such as the applicable rates. There was no circumstance of gross misunderstanding or taking advantage of the other party's distress in this case. Pursuant to Article 175(1) of the Maritime Code of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Maritime Code), which provides that "a salvage contract is concluded when the salvor and the salved party have reached an agreement on the salvage," the salvage contract between Nanhai Rescue Bureau and Investment Company was established. The contract did not violate any mandatory provisions of current laws or regulations, was lawful and valid, and the parties should perform their obligations accordingly.

(2) Whether the cargo owner, China United Oil Co., Ltd., should be added as a third party to the proceedings

The reason Investment Company applied for China United Oil Co., Ltd. to participate in the proceedings was that this case involved the vessel and cargo being in common danger, and according to Article 183 of the Maritime Code, the amount of salvage remuneration should be borne by the owners of the salved vessel and other property in proportion to the respective salved values of the vessel and other property to the total salved value. The first instance court held that Nanhai Rescue Bureau filed its claim based on the salvage contract, seeking payment of salvage fees at the agreed rate; the legal relationship involved in this case and the apportionment of general average expenses claimed by Investment Company pertain to different legal relationships. Therefore, Investment Company's claim to add the cargo owner as a third party to the proceedings could not be sustained.

(3) Whether the salvage carried out by Nanhai Rescue Bureau meets the constitutive requirements of salvage at sea

The "Gabriel" was a vessel as defined in Article 3 of the Maritime Code and was a recognized subject of salvage under the Maritime Code; after the "Gabriel" ran aground, the vessel and its cargo were in a state of danger, with a potential for marine pollution that seriously threatened the safety of the marine environment, and the situation was urgent. The Investment Company and the Shanghai Representative Office were aware of the fact that the "Gabriel" was in maritime danger; the Nanhai Rescue Bureau dispatched the "Nanhai Jiu 116", the "Nanhai Jiu 101", the "Nanhai Jiu 201", and a team of divers to the accident site to provide transportation, guarding, and other services. The above operations were an important component of the successful rescue of the "Gabriel". Although the "Nanhai Jiu 116" did not perform the towing operations as originally agreed, it remained on site under the arrangement of the shipowner to guard the "Gabriel" until it was successfully refloated, and the Maritime Code does not explicitly specify the specific forms of salvage operations. Therefore, the actions taken by the Nanhai Rescue Bureau as described above constituted salvage operations. During the salvage process, the actions or omissions of the Nanhai Rescue Bureau and the Investment Company were entirely voluntary, and there were no circumstances under Article 186 of the Maritime Code that would deprive the salvor of the right to salvage remuneration. From the overall salvage process, the "Gabriel" was successfully refloated, and all crew members and cargo on board ultimately arrived safely at Qinzhou Port and were successfully salved. Accordingly, the salvage operations carried out by the Nanhai Rescue Bureau met the constituent elements of salvage at sea, and it was entitled to receive corresponding salvage remuneration pursuant to Article 179 of the Maritime Code.

(IV) Determination of the amount of salvage remuneration and interest

1. Salvage costs of the "Nanhai Jiu 201"

Regarding the operating time of the "Nanhai Jiu 201", the Investment Company claimed that the Nanhai Rescue Bureau had made additions and deletions to the vessel's deck log, but did not provide evidence to prove this. The three operating periods of the vessel totaled 24.41 hours; the rate of RMB 1.5 per horsepower per hour for the vessel was fully negotiated between the Nanhai Rescue Bureau and the Investment Company, and the court of first instance confirmed it; because the total power of the vessel was 6,093 horsepower, calculated accordingly, the expenses payable by the Investment Company for this vessel were RMB 223,095.20.

2. Costs of the diving team

According to the letter of authorization sent by the Investment Company to the Nanhai Rescue Bureau, the billing period for the diving team's operational fees started from the time the divers boarded the transport vessel and ended when they completed their operations and left the transport vessel to go ashore. Based on this agreement, even if the divers did not enter the water for operations, as long as they boarded the transport vessel, the Investment Company was obligated to pay the Nanhai Rescue Bureau RMB 40,000 for the diving team's operational fees, plus the agreed land dispatch fee of RMB 10,000 and water transportation fee of RMB 55,000, totaling RMB 105,000 for the three items.

3. Salvage costs of the "Nanhai Jiu 116" and the "Nanhai Jiu 101"

The Investment Company did not raise objections to the total power and operating hours of the "Nanhai Jiu 116" and the "Nanhai Jiu 101", but argued that because the two vessels did not actually perform towing operations, the originally agreed rates should be adjusted downward, and could be determined by reference to three rate standards: the "Ministry of Transport of the People's Republic of China Measures for Charges for Salvage Operations on International Routes", the "Ministry of Transport of the People's Republic of China Port Charges Rules", and the "Guangdong Province Port Charges Rules". The court of first instance held that of the standards proposed by the Investment Company, the first standard had been abolished, and the second and third standards applied only to port towing, thus none of the above standards were applicable to this case.

According to Article 180 of the Maritime Code, in determining the remuneration, comprehensive consideration should be given to factors such as the time used by the salvor, expenses incurred, and losses suffered, as well as the liability risks and other risks undertaken by the salvor or its equipment. In actual salvage operations, there are differences in the cost consumption, technical requirements, and liability risks between guarding operations and towing operations. Pursuant to Article 176, Item 2 of the Maritime Code, if the salvage remuneration payable under a contract is manifestly too high or too low compared to the actual salvage services provided, the court or arbitral institution may, during litigation or arbitration, decide or award to modify the salvage contract. Since neither the "Nanhai Jiu 116" nor the "Nanhai Jiu 101" actually performed the towing operations as originally agreed, the Nanhai Rescue Bureau claimed that the salvage rates for the two vessels should still be calculated at the agreed rate of RMB 3.2 per horsepower per hour. The Investment Company argued that the rate was too high and raised an objection. The court of first instance held that an adjustment should be made. On the one hand, in the email correspondence, the Investment Company had repeatedly requested the Nanhai Rescue Bureau to lower the rate, and the Nanhai Rescue Bureau replied by email stating that other expenses arising from the salvage of the "Gabriel" would be discussed later. This indicated that at that time, the Nanhai Rescue Bureau still left room for adjustment of the salvage rate. On the other hand, after the Investment Company changed the salvage plan to lightering and refloating and notified the Nanhai Rescue Bureau of this change, it still inquired in an email on the 15th whether the Nanhai Rescue Bureau could adjust the salvage rate for the vessel to RMB 2.9 per horsepower per hour. This showed that after changing the salvage plan, the Investment Company was still willing to pay at the rate of RMB 2.9 per horsepower per hour, and the determination of this rate was consistent with the principle of encouraging salvage under the Maritime Code. Accordingly, the court of first instance adjusted the salvage rates for the "Nanhai Jiu 116" and the "Nanhai Jiu 101" to RMB 2.9 per horsepower per hour. The salvage costs for the "Nanhai Jiu 116" and the "Nanhai Jiu 101" were accordingly determined as RMB 5,522,467.68 and RMB 742,350.70, respectively.

The salvage costs for the "Nanhai Jiu 116", "Nanhai Jiu 101", "Nanhai Jiu 201", and the diving team totaled RMB 6,592,913.58.

Regarding the interest on the salvage remuneration claimed by the Nanhai Rescue Bureau. The Nanhai Rescue Bureau and the Investment Company did not agree on the payment deadline for the salvage remuneration, nor did they reach a supplementary agreement afterward, and it could not be determined in accordance with relevant contract terms or trade practices. Pursuant to Article 62 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the "Contract Law"), which provides that "where the time limit for performance is not clear, the debtor may perform at any time, and the creditor may also demand performance at any time, but the other party shall be given the necessary time for preparation", the court of first instance, in its discretion, determined that two months after the completion of the salvage operations constituted the preparation time, and accordingly fixed the interest on the salvage remuneration in this case from October 19, 2011, calculated at the PBOC (People's Bank of China) lending rate for working capital for the corresponding period until the date determined for payment in the judgment.

In summary, the court of first instance, after discussion by the judicial committee and pursuant to Articles 175(1), 176(2), 179, and 180 of the Maritime Code, rendered Civil Judgment (2012) Guanghai Fa Chu Zi No. 898, ordering the Investment Company to pay the Nanhai Rescue Bureau salvage remuneration of RMB 6,592,913.58, plus interest at the PBOC lending rate for working capital for the corresponding period from October 19, 2011, until the date determined for payment in the judgment; and dismissing the other claims of the Nanhai Rescue Bureau. The court acceptance fee of RMB 65,822 was borne by the Nanhai Rescue Bureau in the amount of RMB 9,591 and by the Investment Company in the amount of RMB 56,231.

The Investment Company, dissatisfied with the judgment of first instance, filed an appeal, requesting the court of second instance to quash the judgment of first instance, modify the judgment to order the Investment Company to bear corresponding liability at the adjusted rate and in proportion of 38.85%; and order the Nanhai Rescue Bureau to bear the litigation costs of the first and second instances.

During the second instance, except for the determination of the salvage remuneration involved in the case, the parties had no objections to the other facts found by the court of first instance, which were confirmed by the court of second instance.

The court of second instance further found:

After the "Gabriel" ran aground, the master of the vessel reported to the Zhanjiang Maritime Safety Administration, which ordered the master and shipowner to formulate and implement a refloating plan as soon as possible. After study, the shipowner/master decided on the day of the accident to adopt the lightering and refloating plan. To this end, the owner of the "Gabriel" dispatched several shipbuilders, salvage experts, surveyors, etc., from Singapore, the Netherlands, China, and other places to board the vessel for assistance and guidance. Although the "Comprehensive Guarantee Plan for Emergency Lightering and Refloating of the 'Gabriel'" of the Zhanjiang Maritime Safety Administration was issued on August 17, 2011, the lightering and refloating plan had already been confirmed by the master of the "Gabriel" before 14:25 on August 12, 2011, and was approved by the Zhanjiang Maritime Safety Administration.

The salved value of the vessel involved in the case was USD 30,531,856, and the salved value of the cargo was USD 48,053,870. The salved value of the vessel accounted for 38.85% of the total salved value.

The court of second instance held:

(I) Regarding the validity of the salvage contract involved in the case

During the process of negotiating and concluding the salvage contract via email between the Nanhai Rescue Bureau and the Investment Company, the "Gabriel" was in a dangerous situation. The owner of the "Gabriel" entrusted professionals in relevant fields to participate in the study and determination of the salvage plan. The P&I Club and the shipowner also jointly entrusted professional lawyers and maritime professionals to participate in the determination of the salvage plan and the conclusion of the contract involved. The Shanghai Representative Office, as the representative of the shipowner, specifically participated in the negotiation and conclusion of the salvage contract involved. The multiple email exchanges between the Shanghai Representative Office and the Nanhai Rescue Bureau could prove that the Investment Company was fully aware of the on-site situation of the accident and had sufficient professional knowledge of the salvage operations involved. Under the circumstances that it had already chosen the lightering and refloating plan, the Investment Company, after full consultation with the Nanhai Rescue Bureau, finally concluded the contract in this case and agreed to the contract price quoted by the Nanhai Rescue Bureau. The court of second instance did not support the Investment Company's claim that there was a material misunderstanding in the conclusion of the contract involved.

The Investment Company confirmed that, during the same period as the salvage involved, the contract for tug operations signed by the Nanhai Rescue Bureau with a third party showed that the operating fees of the "Nanhai Jiu 116" and similar tugs were not less than RMB 3.0 per horsepower per hour. In this case, there was no circumstance of the Nanhai Rescue Bureau taking advantage of the Investment Company's distress. The Investment Company's argument that the salvage contract involved should be modified or rescinded pursuant to Article 54 of the Contract Law was also untenable.

The Investment Company entrusted the Nanhai Rescue Bureau to dispatch the "Nanhai Jiu 116" and "Nanhai Jiu 101" to the scene to assist in refloating the "Gabriel", and agreed that regardless of whether the assistance in refloating the "Gabriel" was successful, the Investment Company agreed to pay at the rate of RMB 3.2 per horsepower per hour; the "Nanhai Jiu 116" and "Nanhai Jiu 101" were only responsible for towing operations, and the Nanhai Rescue Bureau would not be liable for any accidents during the refloating operation of the "Gabriel". The salvage process in this case also showed that during the participation in the salvage, the Nanhai Rescue Bureau actually followed the instructions of the shipowner. Therefore, the salvage in this case was contractual salvage, where the salvor carried out the salvage under the direction of the salved party. Regardless of whether the salvage was effective, the salved party should, in accordance with Article 179 of the Maritime Code, pay the remuneration based on the manpower and equipment used by the salvor as agreed. The judgment of first instance took the successful refloating of the "Gabriel" and the favorable salvage result as one of the bases for obtaining salvage remuneration in this case, which was an improper application of law.

(II) Whether the salvage remuneration claimed by the Nanhai Rescue Bureau was reasonable

The letter of authorization involved recorded that the Investment Company entrusted the Nanhai Rescue Bureau to dispatch tugs to the scene to assist in refloating the "Gabriel", and also recorded that the "Nanhai Jiu 116" and "Nanhai Jiu 101" were only responsible for towing operations. Towing refloating and lightering refloating were two different and independent salvage methods. Lightering refloating did not necessarily require the guarding of tugs. In addition, when the Investment Company requested the Nanhai Rescue Bureau to dispatch the "Nanhai Jiu 116" and "Nanhai Jiu 101" for salvage, it had not yet decided to adopt the lightering refloating plan. Combined with the wording of the letter of authorization, it should be determined that the purpose of the Investment Company's request to dispatch the tugs to the scene was to use the tugs in an appropriate operational manner to assist in refloating the "Gabriel", rather than to stand by for assistance in refloating. After the tugs arrived at the scene, the Investment Company's salvage plan changed, resulting in neither the tugs nor the divers actually performing the salvage operations agreed in the contract. The Investment Company's request to modify the salvage contract on the grounds that the Nanhai Rescue Bureau had not actually performed the agreed salvage matters was legally well-founded. Given that the court of first instance had already, in response to the Investment Company's claim, comprehensively considered the factors stipulated in Article 180 of the Maritime Code and made adjustments to the salvage remuneration involved, the court of second instance would not make further adjustments. The parties had no objection to the base amount of salvage remuneration of RMB 6,592,913.58 as determined in the judgment of first instance, which was confirmed.

(III) Whether the Investment Company could bear the salvage remuneration involved only in proportion to the vessel's salved value relative to the total salved value

Article 175 of the Maritime Code provides: "The master of a ship in distress shall have the authority to conclude salvage contracts on behalf of the shipowner. The master of a ship in distress or the shipowner shall have the authority to conclude salvage contracts on behalf of the owners of the property on board." Article 183 of the Maritime Code provides: "The amount of salvage remuneration shall be borne by the owners of the salved ship and other property in proportion to the respective salved values of the ship and other property to the total salved value." In the application of the above provisions, the Maritime Code does not distinguish between different types of salvage, so the contractual salvage in this case should also apply. Requiring the shipowner or master to personally sign a salvage contract when a ship is in distress at sea would be detrimental to carrying out salvage promptly and is inconsistent with maritime practice. The two statutory powers of representation set forth in Article 175 of the Maritime Code are not inconsistent with the agency system. Therefore, the Nanhai Rescue Bureau's arguments that the salvage contract in this case was not signed by the master or owner of the "Gabriel", that the Shanghai Representative Office never disclosed to the Nanhai Rescue Bureau that it represented the cargo owner, and that Article 175 of the Maritime Code was inapplicable, were all untenable.

Pursuant to Articles 172 and 179 of the Maritime Code, salvage remuneration is a form of salvage payment. In contractual salvage, the salvor and the salved party may agree on salvage payments, including the form of salvage remuneration. The Nanhai Rescue Bureau's assertion that salvage remuneration applies only to "no cure, no pay" salvage contracts was unfounded. The parties agreed on an economic return for the salved party's performance of its obligations under the contract. The agreed fee should be considered salvage remuneration and should be subject to the provisions of Article 183 of the Maritime Code. Therefore, the Investment Company could bear the salvage remuneration to the Nanhai Rescue Bureau only in proportion to the vessel's salved value relative to the total salved value, i.e., 38.85%. The amount of salvage remuneration to be borne by the Investment Company was RMB 2,561,346.93. The Investment Company's failure to pay the salvage remuneration to the Nanhai Rescue Bureau constituted a breach of contract. The Nanhai Rescue Bureau's claim for interest on the delayed payment was legally well-founded and should be supported. The court of first instance's discretionary determination that the Investment Company should pay the remuneration within two months after receiving notice was reasonable. Therefore, the interest in this case should be calculated from October 19, 2011, at the PBOC lending rate for working capital for the corresponding period until the date determined for payment in the judgment.

In summary, the court of second instance, pursuant to Articles 175 and 183 of the Maritime Code, Article 107 of the Contract Law, and Articles 64 and 170(1)(2) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, rendered Civil Judgment (2014) Yue Gao Fa Min Si Zhong Zi No. 117, quashing the judgment of first instance; ordering the Investment Company to pay the Nanhai Rescue Bureau salvage remuneration of RMB 2,561,346.93, plus interest at the PBOC lending rate for working capital for the corresponding period from October 19, 2011, until the date determined for payment in the judgment; and dismissing the other claims of the Nanhai Rescue Bureau. The court acceptance fee of RMB 65,822 for the second instance was borne by the Investment Company in the amount of RMB 23,283.11 and by the Nanhai Rescue Bureau in the amount of RMB 42,538.89.

The Nanhai Rescue Bureau, dissatisfied with the judgment of second instance, applied for retrial, alleging: (1) The letter of authorization of the Investment Company recorded that regardless of whether the assistance in refloating the "Gabriel" was successful, the Investment Company agreed to pay at the rate of RMB 3.2 per horsepower per hour, indicating that the parties had agreed in advance on the calculation of the rate, etc., and the Nanhai Rescue Bureau had provided services such as salvage, guarding, and transportation as agreed, and the contract between the parties had been legally formed and performed. The court of second instance only ordered the Investment Company to pay 38.85% of the salvage costs, which violated the privity of contract and was inconsistent with the basic principle of full performance of contractual obligations. (2) The "Guarantee Letter for General Average" submitted by the Nanhai Rescue Bureau at the time of application for retrial could prove that on August 18, 2011, the insurer of the cargo had guaranteed to bear the salvage costs to be apportioned by the cargo owner, but the judgment of second instance did not find this fact and only ordered the Investment Company to pay part of the contract fees, which reduced the salvage costs ultimately to be borne by the shipowner and the cargo owner, and was also detrimental to achieving the purpose of the International Convention on Salvage 1989 (hereinafter referred to as the "Salvage Convention") to encourage salvage operations at sea. This evidence was sufficient to overturn the judgment of second instance. (3) As the Nanhai Rescue Bureau, a national professional maritime salvage organization, having participated in the salvage of the "Gabriel", was entitled to obtain the full salvage remuneration under the contract as agreed. The judgment of second instance deprived the Nanhai Rescue Bureau of its lawful rights and interests under the contract, which was inconsistent with the public interest of encouraging salvage at sea. (4) The contract involved in this case calculated salvage remuneration based on the agreed rate and fees and constituted an employed salvage contract. Even if the fees under this contract were considered salvage remuneration under the law of salvage at sea, the Investment Company was obligated, pursuant to Article 188 of the Maritime Code, to require the cargo owner to provide security to the salvor, i.e., the Nanhai Rescue Bureau, rather than, as the Investment Company did in this case, requiring the cargo insurer to provide security to the Investment Company. In summary, the Nanhai Rescue Bureau requested that the judgment of second instance be quashed, and that the Investment Company be ordered to pay the fees under the salvage contract in the amount of RMB 6,592,913.58 and the corresponding interest, and that the litigation costs of the first and second instances be borne by the Investment Company.

Investment Company responded: (1) The judgment of the court of second instance, ordering the Investment Company to pay salvage remuneration in proportion to the value of the ship saved as a proportion of the total value saved, adhered to the principle of privity of contract and correctly applied the law. First, Article 6 of the Salvage Convention and Article 175 of the Maritime Code confer two statutory representative authorities upon the master and the shipowner. The salvage contract in question was concluded by the Investment Company on behalf of the cargo owners jointly with the Nanhai Rescue Bureau, with the Investment Company and the cargo owners both being Party A to the contract; second, Article 183 of the Maritime Code does not expressly provide that the remuneration it governs applies only to "no cure, no pay" salvage contracts and not to engagement salvage contracts. The salvage remuneration to which the Nanhai Rescue Bureau is entitled falls within the scope of adjustment of Article 183 of the Maritime Code. The proviso in Article 179 of the Maritime Code, "unless otherwise agreed in the contract," has already provided for the institutional design and regulation of engagement salvage. The salvor and the salvors may agree that the entitlement to salvage remuneration is not linked to the result of the salvage, and regardless of whether the salvage is successful, the salvor may claim salvage payments (including salvage remuneration, reward, or compensation) at the agreed fixed rate. The salvage in this case was property salvage, and the remuneration obtained by the Nanhai Rescue Bureau should be, and can only be, the salvage remuneration provided for in the Maritime Code. (2) At the beginning of the salvage, before the filing of this lawsuit, or at the latest before the conclusion of the court of second instance hearing, the Nanhai Rescue Bureau should have discovered the existence of the "Average Guarantee," but the Nanhai Rescue Bureau did not discover this evidence until after the conclusion of the second instance. This was due to its subjective negligence, not objective reasons, and this evidence does not constitute new evidence. Even if the "Average Guarantee" constitutes new evidence, the Nanhai Rescue Bureau's request based on this evidence that the Investment Company pay the full amount of salvage remuneration is entirely unfounded. This is because the judgment of the second instance ordered the Investment Company to pay its own share based on the proportion of the ship's salved value, and does not involve the part that should be borne by the cargo owners as guaranteed by the "Average Guarantee." The "Average Guarantee" and the second instance judgment neither require the shipowner to advance the salvage remuneration on behalf of the cargo owners, nor deprive the Nanhai Rescue Bureau of the right to demand payment from the cargo owners in proportion, nor relieve the cargo owners of this obligation. (3) General average and marine salvage are two independent systems. The rules of general average adjustment cannot be used to deprive the Investment Company of its statutory right to pay salvage remuneration only in proportion. (4) Because the Zhanjiang Maritime Safety Administration instructed the salvage plan to be changed from towing and refloating to lightering and refloating by transshipment, if the originally agreed rate for towing operations (3.2 yuan per horsepower hour) continued to be applied, it would be manifestly unfair. According to the principle of change of circumstances, this rate should be changed or adjusted. Additionally, the Nanhai Rescue Bureau, as a public institution, should, to safeguard the public interest, only collect remuneration sufficient to cover actual expenses, and should not make excessive profits. Furthermore, performing life salvage is its primary administrative duty and should not collect any remuneration. Even for the adjusted salvage remuneration, the proportion attributable to life salvage (at least 50%) should be further deducted. In summary, the Investment Company requests the rejection of the Nanhai Rescue Bureau's retrial application and the upholding of the second instance judgment.

The Shanghai Representative Office's statement of opinion is the same as the Investment Company's response opinion.

Upon trial, this Court confirms the facts found by the courts of first and second instance.

Opinion of the Court:

This case is a dispute over a marine salvage contract. The People's Republic of China is a party to the Salvage Convention. The purposes established by the Salvage Convention, namely, to encourage timely and effective salvage of vessels and other property in danger, as well as events that pose a threat to environmental safety, while ensuring adequate encouragement for personnel performing salvage operations, should be followed in this case. After the incident in question occurred, the Investment Company promptly sought salvage, and the Nanhai Rescue Bureau actively participated in the salvage as agreed, both playing a role in preventing marine pollution, which is commendable.

As the Investment Company is a Greek company and the vessel "Gabriel" is a Greek-flagged oil tanker, this case contains foreign-related elements. All parties consistently chose to apply the laws of the People's Republic of China during the proceedings. In accordance with Article 3 of the Law of the People's Republic of China on the Application of Laws to Foreign-Related Civil Relations, this Court applies the laws of the People's Republic of China to adjudicate this case. The Maritime Code, as a special law governing maritime transport relations and ship relations, shall prevail. Matters not provided for in the Maritime Code shall be governed by the relevant provisions of the Contract Law and other related laws.

Based on the reasons for retrial submitted by the Nanhai Rescue Bureau and the responses of the Investment Company and the Shanghai Representative Office, the issues in dispute in this case involve both factual and legal application aspects. Specifically, they include: (1) Whether the evidentiary materials submitted by the Nanhai Rescue Bureau at the retrial stage constitute new evidence as defined by law, and if so, whether they are sufficient to overturn the second instance judgment; (2) How to understand the salvage contracts stipulated in the Salvage Convention and the Maritime Code; (3) The nature and applicable law of the contract involved in this case; (4) How to determine the amount of salvage remuneration claimed by the Nanhai Rescue Bureau.

(1) Regarding whether the evidentiary materials submitted by the Nanhai Rescue Bureau constitute new evidence as defined by law and whether they are sufficient to overturn the second instance judgment

During the retrial application period, the Nanhai Rescue Bureau submitted to this Court the "Average Guarantee" issued by the Beijing Branch of the People's Insurance Company of China (Property Insurance) (hereinafter referred to as PICC Property Insurance Beijing Branch), aiming to prove that after the Investment Company pays the remuneration to the Nanhai Rescue Bureau, it can obtain compensation from PICC Property Insurance Beijing Branch, and believed that this evidence was sufficient to overturn the second instance judgment. The Investment Company and the Shanghai Representative Office stated during the trial that they had no objection to the authenticity and legality of this evidentiary material, but argued that this evidentiary material was not new evidence and did not recognize its probative effect.

This Court holds that this evidentiary material was issued by PICC Property Insurance Beijing Branch to the owner of the vessel "Gabriel" and other possible interested parties in the voyage. Although this evidentiary material is helpful for this Court to understand the relevant circumstances of the assumption of salvage payment in the case, it is not directly related to the salvage remuneration dispute between the parties in this case and is therefore not adopted.

(2) Regarding how to understand the salvage contracts stipulated in the Salvage Convention and the Maritime Code

Marine salvage is a traditional international maritime legal system, specifically provided for in the Salvage Convention and the Maritime Code. The provisions of Chapter 9 of the Maritime Code on marine salvage have borrowed and absorbed the main content of the Salvage Convention. Article 12 of the Salvage Convention and Article 179 of the Maritime Code stipulate the principle of "no cure, no pay" for the payment of salvage remuneration. Articles 13 of the Salvage Convention and Articles 180 and 183 of the Maritime Code further provide for the criteria for assessing remuneration and its specific allocation based on this principle. The above provisions are specific regulations on salvage contracts where the parties determine salvage remuneration based on the principle of "no cure, no pay." At the same time, both the Salvage Convention and the Maritime Code permit the parties to otherwise agree on the determination of salvage remuneration. Therefore, in addition to the "no cure, no pay" salvage contracts stipulated in the Salvage Convention and the Maritime Code, engagement salvage contracts may also be formed based on the parties' agreement.

(3) Regarding the nature and applicable law of the contract involved in this case

Based on the facts found in this case, after full negotiation between the Investment Company and the Nanhai Rescue Bureau, it was explicitly agreed that the Investment Company would pay remuneration regardless of whether the salvage was successful, and that the Nanhai Rescue Bureau would not be liable for any accidents occurring during the refloating operations of the vessel "Gabriel." According to this agreement, whether the Nanhai Rescue Bureau obtains salvage remuneration is not directly linked to the actual effect of the salvage, and the calculation of salvage remuneration is based on agreed fixed rates per horsepower hour of the salvage vessel and labor input, etc., and is unrelated to the value of the salved property. Therefore, the salvage contract involved in this case does not belong to the "no cure, no pay" salvage contracts stipulated in the Salvage Convention and the Maritime Code, but constitutes an engagement salvage contract.

Regarding the conditions and standards for payment of remuneration under an engagement salvage contract, the Salvage Convention and the Maritime Code do not provide specific provisions. The courts of first and second instance adjusted the fixed rate agreed upon by the parties in the engagement salvage contract based on relevant factors stipulated in Article 180 of the Maritime Code, which was an erroneous application of law. This case should be governed and determined in accordance with the relevant provisions of the Contract Law regarding the rights and obligations of the parties.

(4) Regarding how to determine the amount of salvage remuneration claimed by the Nanhai Rescue Bureau

Regarding the amount of salvage remuneration claimed by the Nanhai Rescue Bureau, the Investment Company argues that it should bear the salvage remuneration in accordance with Article 183 of the Maritime Code, based on the proportion of the value of the salved ship to the total value of all salved property. This Court holds that Article 183 of the Maritime Code should apply to "no cure, no pay" salvage contracts, while the contract in question is an engagement salvage contract. It is not improper for the Nanhai Rescue Bureau to demand full payment of the agreed salvage remuneration from the Investment Company based on the contract it concluded with the Investment Company.

The Investment Company also argued that the change of the salvage plan from the initial towing and underwater search operations to lightering by transshipment constituted a change of circumstances, and the previously agreed salvage remuneration rate should be adjusted. This Court holds that Article 26 of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation (II) on Several Issues concerning the Application of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China stipulates: "If, after the formation of a contract, there occurs a significant change in objective circumstances that was unforeseeable by the parties at the time of contracting, is not force majeure, and does not constitute a commercial risk, and continuing to perform the contract would be manifestly unfair to one party or would defeat the purpose of the contract, and the party requests the people's court to modify or terminate the contract, the people's court shall determine whether to modify or terminate the contract based on the principle of fairness and in light of the actual circumstances of the case." The adjustment of the salvage plan in this case was not based on a significant change in objective circumstances, but was the result of negotiations and discussions among relevant parties, including the parties themselves. Furthermore, continuing to perform the contract is not manifestly unfair to the Investment Company, nor does it defeat the purpose of the contract. The adjustment of the salvage plan does not constitute a change of circumstances in the legal sense. The Investment Company's claim for reducing the agreed rates and fees based on this ground lacks factual and legal basis and is not supported by this Court.

The Nanhai Rescue Bureau, in accordance with its agreement with the Investment Company, deployed corresponding vessels and personnel for the salvage services involved. The Investment Company should pay remuneration based on the agreed rates and the vessels, personnel, and time expended by the Nanhai Rescue Bureau. The first instance judgment correctly determined, in accordance with the parties' agreement, that the Investment Company should pay the Nanhai Rescue Bureau the costs for the vessel "Nanhaijiu 201" and the diving team. At the same time, the first instance judgment, based on the actual salvage situation, reduced the salvage rate for the vessels "Nanhaijiu 116" and "Nanhaijiu 101" from 3.2 yuan per horsepower hour to 2.9 yuan per horsepower hour. The Nanhai Rescue Bureau did not appeal this and also did not raise this issue in its retrial request. This Court approves.

In summary, the court of second instance, using the amount of salvage remuneration determined in the first instance judgment as the base, and in accordance with the provisions of the Maritime Code, ordered the Investment Company to pay salvage remuneration in proportion to the value of the vessel saved as a proportion of the total saved property. The application of the law and the result of the judgment were erroneous and should be corrected. The first instance judgment was erroneous in its application of the law, but given that the adjustment of the relevant rate in the first instance judgment was based on the parties' contractual agreement, and the Nanhai Rescue Bureau did not exercise its relevant litigation rights to object, the result of the first instance judgment may be upheld. Pursuant to Article 8 and Article 107 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, Item 2 of Paragraph 1 of Article 170 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, and Paragraph 1 of Article 407 of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, this Court renders judgment as follows:

1. The civil judgment of the Guangdong High People's Court (2014) Yue Gao Fa Min Si Zhong Zi No. 117 is reversed;

2. The civil judgment of the Guangzhou Maritime Court (2012) Guang Hai Fa Chu Zi No. 898 is affirmed.

The court fee for first instance is 65,822 yuan, with 9,591 yuan to be borne by the Nanhai Rescue Bureau of the Ministry of Transport, and 56,231 yuan to be borne by Archangelos Investments Co., Ltd. The court fee for second instance is 65,822 yuan, to be borne by Archangelos Investments Co., Ltd.

This judgment is final.
